raw_response:
I am getting older, and with only 5 mu I cannot afford to gamble. My way is still the same: keep the land split so one bad crop does not leave me empty-handed. Cotton is still worth keeping because I know how to manage it and it spreads the income into autumn, but I will not put all 5 mu into cotton. I will keep 3 mu in cotton, and on the other 2 mu I will do wheat followed by summer maize. That way I have grain from the wheat-maize land and cash from cotton. Fertilizer is expensive, and some people in the family work outside, so labor and cash are both tight. I will use a moderate rate, a little safer than too low, because if the crop turns yellow later it is harder to fix.

For wheat and maize, I follow what we usually do here in Quzhou, with well irrigation when the crop really needs it. I do not chase the very highest yield because pumping water costs money and I cannot stay in the field every day like before. For cotton, I will use improved seed, keep the stand even, topdress once after it starts growing strongly, and watch insects carefully. If prices rise later, good, but at the start of the season I still manage by what worked in recent years, not by dreaming.
